summary.text: IMD is a network of AI agents that you can hire for jobs such as building and hosting a website, writing a researched report, or giving a signed answer a smart contract can use.
You describe what you want in plain words, and other agents review the work before it is delivered.
The agents run on the own machines of people who hold one of 2,000 seat NFTs, and a news site reported that those holders pay for the computing power.
Opening a job costs half an IMD token, paid from a wallet, either on the explorer's launch page or straight through the project's request contract.
The project's trading pool charges a 1% swap fee and says it burns most of the tokens it removes, and a contributor says launch fees also feed the burn.
A news site names a person who posts as Adam as the creator, and a second person says they contribute; the creator has posted that there are no employees.
One thing is unclear: the project's docs say its contract code is not verified, while a block explorer shows the token as verified.

open_questions: Which X accounts, if any, does a contract, ENS record or deployer wallet point to? None was found, so @surfcoderepeat and @taylor_ have tie none.
What does an operator typically pay for a seat, an AI plan and the machine that runs it?
Panel answer A3 says @surfcoderepeat posted that tokens launched through the swarm can be paired with imdusd; the post itself was not read, so no line was written.
What is the circulating IMD supply across all chains after counting tokens locked in the Base bridge?
Who controls the deployer wallet, and which deployed contracts are still in use?
notes: Earlier reports F1, F2, F3 were carried forward and merged; panel answers A1 to A3 were used as given (their pages were not reopened). Decision on the open question from the earlier stopped run: the brief's 40-line and 8-claim limits were kept, because they are the brief's specific hard limits; eligible earlier lines that did not fit were listed in dropped with the reason. Claims include all lines from personal X posts and articles. Lines F3 took from the Identity-md GitHub repository were treated as claims at most, because that channel has no strong or weak tie. State reads were rechecked on 2026-11-19 at Ethereum block 26,451,648 via ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com: job price, seat cap and count, ENS records and POOL4 hook owner matched earlier reports; total supply had fallen from the earlier reading, consistent with burns. A1 (docs price a job at 0.5 IMD, true) confirms m-1; A2 (docs price a job at 5 IMD, false) agrees with m-1 and no line says 5 IMD. The ENS name identitymd.eth gives strong ties to the two API hosts. The site, docs and POOL4 docs have weak ties because they publish the main contract address. Token amounts in text are whole IMD; raw values are in fact.
